title: 月夜忆舍弟
titleEn: Thinking of My Brothers on a Moonlit Night
author: 杜甫
intro: War has scattered Du Fu's family, and he has no idea whether his brothers are alive. One of its lines — “the moon is brighter over home” — is still how Chinese people talk about missing where they come from.
analysis: 这首诗写于战乱年代。开头两句先写环境：守边的战鼓一响，路上就没有行人了；秋天的边地，只听见一只孤雁在叫。孤雁离开了雁群，正像诗人和弟弟们分散在各地。第三、四句最有名：“露从今夜白”，点出这天是白露节气；“月是故乡明”，月亮哪里都一样，诗人却偏说故乡的更亮——这是心里的感觉，不是事实，所以特别动人。后四句直接说出痛苦：弟弟们都分散了，家也没有了，连打听他们是死是活都没地方问；寄出的信常常收不到，何况战争还没停。全诗从景写到情，越写越沉重。
analysisEn: Du Fu wrote this during the An Lushan Rebellion, when the war had split his family apart. The opening sets the scene: the drums of the garrison have sounded, so no one is out on the roads, and over the autumn frontier there is only the call of a single wild goose. A goose that has lost its flock is an obvious picture of the poet himself, cut off from his brothers. The next couplet is the famous one. “From tonight the dew turns white” tells us it is the White Dew solar term in early autumn; “the moon is brighter over home” is not a fact but a feeling — the same moon shines everywhere, yet the one over home seems clearer to him. The second half speaks plainly. His brothers are scattered, the family home is gone, and there is nowhere even to ask whether they are alive or dead. Letters rarely get through, and the fighting has not stopped. The poem moves from landscape to grief, and each couplet weighs more than the last.
background: Du Fu (712–770), often called the “Sage of Poetry”, lived through the An Lushan Rebellion and wrote more about war and ordinary suffering than any poet of his age. This poem is usually dated to autumn 759, when he was in Qinzhou (in today's Gansu) and his younger brothers were scattered in the war zones of the east.
pronunciation: 戍 shù（守边）；人行 xíng；长不达 cháng（常常，不读 zhǎng）；舍弟 shè（谦称自己的弟弟）。
version: 采用通行教材版本。第二句有的版本作“秋边一雁声”，通行作“边秋一雁声”。

lines.lit: The garrison drums cut off people's travel;
lines.en: The watch-drums sound, and the roads go empty;

lines.lit: frontier autumn: the cry of one wild goose.
lines.en: one wild goose calls across the frontier autumn.

lines.lit: The dew from tonight is white;
lines.en: From tonight the dew turns white —

lines.lit: the moon is the home village's bright one.
lines.en: and the moon is brighter over home.

lines.lit: I have brothers, all scattered apart;
lines.en: My brothers are scattered far and wide,

lines.lit: no home where I can ask of death or life.
lines.en: and with no home left, who can I ask if they live?

lines.lit: Letters I send often do not arrive;
lines.en: The letters I send seldom reach them,

lines.lit: all the more since the fighting has not stopped.
lines.en: and still the soldiers are not sent home.

words.note: 古代对别人谦称自己的弟弟；现代汉语一般直接说“我弟弟”。
“戍”是守边，今天还有“戍边”一词；戍鼓响起表示宵禁，路上不许走人。

words.en: to stop all travel on the roads
words.note: “断”是隔断；现代汉语说“没人走了”“断了行人”。

words.en: from tonight the dew turns white
words.note: 指二十四节气里的“白露”，今天还用这个节气名，在九月上旬。
现代汉语也常用。“月是故乡明”今天常被引用来表达思乡。
现代汉语说“都”；书面语还有“皆大欢喜”。

words.en: to ask whether someone is alive or dead
words.note: 现代汉语一般说“生死”，诗里为了押韵和平仄说“死生”。
古义是书信，和今天“书本”的“书”不同；“家书”就是家信。
这里通“常”，是“常常”的意思。

words.en: all the more so; what's more

words.note: 停止战争；现代汉语说“停战”“休战”。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月亮本来到处一样亮，诗人偏说故乡的更明，写出了想家的心情。
imagery.en: The moon is the same everywhere, but he insists it shines brighter over home — homesickness changing what he sees.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 一只离群的孤雁，正像和兄弟分散、孤身在外的诗人。
imagery.en: A single goose that has lost its flock — just like the poet, cut off from his brothers.

imagery.name: 露
imagery.zh: 白露点明季节已是深秋前后，带出寒意和凄凉。
imagery.en: White dew marks the turn into autumn and brings in a sense of cold and desolation.
